paragraphs: At twelve o'clock, Leo and Mia sat down at a canteen table. Each child carried a blue lunch box. They put the boxes on the table, and they talked about the morning. Leo was hungry, and Mia was hungry, too. The boxes looked the same, so they picked up the wrong ones.

Mia opened the box in front of her. It was untidy. She saw a cheese sandwich with butter and a piece of bread with jam. There was also a banana, a small bag of cereal, and a bag of olives. "I don't like olives," said Mia. Leo opened the other box. He looked inside with wide eyes. It was tidy. There was rice, an egg with a little salt, an apple, and a fork.

"I like apples, but I don't like eggs," said Leo. "Yuck, an egg!" he said. Lily sat at the next table. "Leo, that is unkind," said Lily. "Sorry, Mia," said Leo. Mia smiled and looked at the two boxes. The boxes were the same, but the foods were not. "These are not our lunches," she said.

"Do you like cheese?" asked Leo. "Of course," said Mia. "Do you like rice?" she asked. "Yes, I do," said Leo. Mia liked cheese and Leo liked rice, so they kept those foods. Mia ate her sandwich without the olives. "You can have the egg if you want, Mia," said Leo. Mia liked eggs, so she took it. Leo liked olives, so Mia gave him the bag. Then they ate and talked together. Teacher Kim saw them and smiled. "What a good idea," she said.
